# KafkaProduceLatencyHigh

<!-- GENERATED by monitoring/dashgen from internal/rules (make alerts). Do not edit. -->

| Severity | Component | Dashboard | for (production / demo) |
|---|---|---|---|
| warning | kafka | [kafka-broker](http://grafana.localhost:8080/d/kafka-broker/) | 10m / 1m |

**Summary:** Produce p99 latency on broker <kafka_broker> is above 500 ms

The broker needs more than 500 ms for 1 % of produce requests. Open the request time breakdown: request queue = handler saturation, local = disk, remote = slow followers (acks=all).

## Impact

Producers wait longer for acknowledgements; with max.in.flight limits throughput drops and buffers fill (producer-side timeouts).

## Diagnosis

1. Kafka · Broker Deep Dive → 'Where does Produce time go?': request queue (handler saturation), local (disk), remote (waiting for followers, acks=all), response queue/send (network threads).
2. Correlate with ISR shrinks, GC pauses and disk I/O pressure of the same broker.

## Mitigation

- Remote dominant: fix the slow follower (see KafkaUnderReplicatedPartitions).
- Local dominant: disk is too slow — check I/O PSI and log flush latency.
- Request queue dominant: see KafkaRequestHandlerSaturated.

## Expression

```promql
max by (kafka_cluster, kafka_broker) (kafka_network_requestmetrics_totaltimems{request="Produce",quantile="0.99"}) > 500
```
